name: Motorcycle Maintenance Checklist
description: Routine motorcycle upkeep grouped by interval — every ride, monthly, and at major service points — covering oil, chain, tires, brakes and filters.

items.text: Check tire pressure when cold and inspect tread
Confirm brakes feel firm and respond normally
Test all lights and the horn
Glance under the bike for leaks
Check chain or belt tension and lubrication
Check oil level and condition on level ground when warm
Change engine oil at the manual's interval
items.note: Use the grade and capacity specified for your model

items.text: Replace the oil filter with each oil change
Inspect for oil leaks around the drain plug and gaskets
Reset the service reminder if your bike has one
Clean the chain with a suitable cleaner
Lubricate the chain after cleaning and before storage
Adjust chain slack to the spec in your manual
Inspect sprockets for hooked or worn teeth
Check the belt for cracks or shaft drive oil if fitted
Measure brake pad thickness and replace before the wear limit
Check brake fluid level and condition; flush per schedule
Inspect rotors and brake lines for wear or damage
Replace tires that are worn, cracked or aged
Check wheel bearings and spoke tension
Clean or replace the air filter per the schedule
Check and top up coolant if liquid cooled
Replace coolant at the recommended interval
Inspect the fuel system and replace the fuel filter if specified
Service the spark plugs at the recommended mileage
Check and torque key fasteners to spec
Lubricate cables, levers and pivot points
Inspect suspension for leaks and correct sag
Test the battery and clean the terminals
Adjust steering head and wheel bearings if needed

faq.q: How often should I change motorcycle oil?
faq.a: Follow the interval in your owner's manual, which is typically based on mileage and time. Many bikes call for an oil and filter change every few thousand miles or at least once a season, and severe riding conditions shorten that interval.

faq.q: How do I keep the chain in good shape?
faq.a: Clean and lubricate the chain regularly, check tension and adjust it to the spec in your manual, and inspect the chain and sprockets for wear. A well-kept chain runs smoother, lasts longer and improves safety.

faq.q: What should I check every month?
faq.a: Tire pressure and condition, brake pad wear and fluid levels, lights, chain tension and lubrication, and any fresh leaks. Monthly attention catches slow problems before they leave you stranded or cause a failure on the road.

faq.q: Should I follow the manual or this checklist?
faq.a: Always follow your owner's manual and the manufacturer's maintenance schedule first, since intervals and specs vary by model. Use this checklist as a general supplement and hand complex jobs to a qualified mechanic.

faq.q: Can I print this motorcycle maintenance checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it with your tools and log the date and mileage each time you service the bike.
